summary: Iteration 6 — full end-to-end test of the new Marketing module + default-password onboarding. All 20 backend pytest tests pass and every requested frontend flow works. No blocking bugs found.
critical_code_review_comments: TeamTab.jsx AddUserDialog initial state defaults roles to ['crew']. When the tester (or a real owner) wants a marketing-only user, they must remember to uncheck 'crew' first. Recommend either (a) starting with roles=[] so the operator has to pick, or (b) making the checkboxes single-select via a radio-like affordance, so that clicking 'marketing' auto-unchecks 'crew'. During QA I initially only added marketing while leaving crew checked and the created user landed on /today (crew nav) instead of /marketing because the backend uses roles[0] ('crew') as the primary role.

server.py create_user sets role from the first item of the roles list (roles[0]) — the ordering of the array from the frontend determines the user's landing page. Consider making 'primary_role' explicit or preferring 'marketing'/'owner' over 'crew' when a user has multiple roles, to remove this footgun.

MarketingDashboard.jsx uses window.location for date range presets is fine, but the 'mkt-airtable-banner' text is duplicated with the global 'Airtable key needed' banner in Layout — two amber banners appear together on /marketing. Not a bug, minor UX polish.
